title: Partner Co-sell Pipeline Review - Vanguard Integrations
summary: Quarterly co-sell pipeline review focusing on three mutual opportunities. Discussed qualification, technical blockers (VPC, SSO), upcoming joint exec briefing, and next steps for pricing and security docs. Agreed to run a short benchmark on performance and share joint deck.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off on time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lina: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to sync.
[00:12] Priya: Great, we'll run through the three deals then call out next steps. Please jump in if I talk too fast.
[00:20] Marco: Sounds good.
[00:28] Jordan: First up is Project Orion, quick status — you have champion lined up, expected close Q1, roughly $600k ARR if all goes well?
[00:36] Lina: Yeah that's correct, champion is product lead, but legal timeline could push. They asked about private deployment and audit logs.
[00:44] Priya: For audit logs and SOC2, Redwood Private is an option, and we have an enterprise compliance pack. I'll put the security brief in the notes.
[00:53] Marco: One thing from tech: they want VPC peering, are we able to support VPC with dedicated? Heard something about on-prem package.
[01:02] Priya: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem. There's some onboarding work but doable. Note — our workbook for VPC setup has a few checklist items: firewall rules, KMS keys, and subnets.
[01:15] Jordan: Okay, action item there to share the VPC checklist.
[01:20] Lina: Good.
[01:24] Jordan: Next, Project Borealis, mid-stage, $250k, main ask is predictable latency for chat customer support use cases. They were concerned about batching causing latency spikes.
[01:36] Priya: Right — for low-latency we recommended dedicated pools with autoscale and smaller batch sizes, also prefix caching for common prompts. We'll put perf profiles in the deck. There was a note in the doc about quantization tradeoffs too, some customers saw quality changes when heavy quantization used.
[01:51] Marco: Do we have benchmark numbers we can share quickly? The prospect wants 50–200ms p95 for shorter contexts.
[01:59] Priya: We can run a short benchmark on our side and share results. Might need sample prompt sets.
[02:05] Jordan: Marco, can you get us their sample prompts or allow a small test dataset?
[02:09] Marco: Yep, I'll follow up.
[02:12] Lina: On pricing, they asked about committed vs pay-as-you-go. They prefer committed for predictability but want price protection.
[02:20] Jordan: For committed we can put together a term sheet; include burst capacity notes. We'll send a draft.
[02:26] Sofia: Quick note — legal will want data residency language, especially for EU customers. Do you have region controls?
[02:33] Priya: Yes, region pinning is possible in Redwood Dedicated and Private. We'll include the region controls doc link.
[02:40] Jordan: Last deal is Project Meridian, bigger logo but longer sales cycle, potential $1.2M ARR over three years but they need an executive briefing with SRE + security.
[02:51] Lina: They want joint exec brief where Vanguard introduces Redwood as preferred inference provider. We need a slide deck and talking points.
[02:58] Jordan: We'll prepare a joint deck. Priya, can you lead the technical slide content?
[03:03] Priya: Sure, I'll draft slides on runtime performance, fallback policies, and KV caching.
[03:09] Marco: Any red flags on compliance? They requested HSM support for KMS.
[03:14] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS and support HSM-backed keys in our Private offering. We'll note required lead time for key rotation and HSM provisioning.
[03:25] Lina: Excellent.
[03:28] Jordan: Okay, a few cross-deal notes: 1) Need to align on who owns which stage of the coop motion — Vanguard handles intro and first few meetings, Redwood takes technical deep-dive and pilot. 2) Pricing to be jointly agreed, 3) We'll maintain a shared pipeline spreadsheet.
[03:45] Marco: On the coop motion, let's make a simple RACI in the shared sheet.
[03:50] Jordan: Agreed, we'll add RACI.
[03:53] Priya: Quick hiccup — we've seen confusion between Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private in previous deals; need to be explicit on tradeoffs (hosted vs private, latency/cost/scope).
[04:05] Lina: Yes please, our reps sometimes mix them up.
[04:09] Jordan: We'll add a one-pager.
[04:12] Sofia: Also ask — any competitor intel? The prospects mentioned Anthropic for safety controls and Seldon for on-prem orchestration.
[04:19] Jordan: Noted.
[04:21] Priya: To wrap, timeline-wise: share pricing draft and security docs by Thursday, run benchmark next week, schedule exec brief for Project Meridian in two weeks.
[04:31] Lina: Good.
[04:33] Jordan: Anything else?
[04:36] Marco: No, that's it from me.
[04:38] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the shared spreadsheet link and action items.
[04:45] (call ends)
action_items: Jordan Kim - Share VPC checklist and region controls doc - 2026-11-12
Priya Desai - Draft technical slides for joint exec brief (runtime, KV caching, fallback) - 2026-11-18
Marco Ruiz - Provide sample prompt set for Borealis benchmark - 2026-11-11
Jordan Kim - Draft committed pricing term sheet for Project Borealis - 2026-11-13
next_steps: Jordan to upload partner co-sell spreadsheet and RACI link
Redwood to run short performance benchmark next week and share results
Redwood to send security/compliance pack including SOC2/HSM/KMS notes
Schedule joint exec briefing for Project Meridian (target: 2 weeks)
